content: 1. Erythromycin stearate increases the levels or effects of maraviroc by inhibiting hepatic and intestinal CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid coadministration or use an alternative drug. 2. Marijuana increases the levels or effects of erythromycin stearate by inhibiting hepatic and intestinal CYP3A4 metabolism. This combination is contraindicated. Monitor closely if unavoidable. 3. Erythromycin stearate increases the levels or effects of mavacamten by inhibiting hepatic and intestinal CYP3A4 metabolism. Therapy modification or close monitoring is required. Initiation of moderate CYP3A4 inhibitors may necessitate a reduced mavacamten dose. 4. Mavorixafor increases the levels or effects of erythromycin stearate by inhibiting P-glycoprotein (MDR1) efflux transporters. Use caution and monitor closely. 5. Erythromycin stearate increases the levels or effects of mavorixafor by inhibiting hepatic and intestinal CYP3A4 metabolism. Therapy modification or close monitoring is required. Monitor for adverse effects of mavorixafor when coadministered with moderate CYP3A4 inhibitors. 6. Both erythromycin stearate and mavorixafor prolong the QTc interval. Therapy modification or close monitoring is necessary. Mavorixafor causes concentration-dependent QTc prolongation, so QTc monitoring is recommended in patients with risk factors for QTc prolongation. 7. Erythromycin stearate increases the levels or effects of mefloquine by inhibiting hepatic and intestinal CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor closely. 8. Erythromycin stearate increases the levels or effects of mestranol by inhibiting P-glycoprotein (MDR1) efflux transporters. It also decreases mestranol levels by altering intestinal flora, which applies only to oral forms of the hormone. There is a low risk of contraceptive failure. 9. Erythromycin stearate increases the levels or effects of methadone by inhibiting hepatic and intestinal CYP3A4 metabolism. Both drugs prolong the QTc interval. Avoid coadministration or use an alternative drug. 10. Erythromycin stearate increases the levels or effects of methylprednisolone by inhibiting P-glycoprotein (MDR1) efflux transporters and decreasing its metabolism. Use an alternative drug if possible. 11. Metronidazole increases the levels or effects of erythromycin stearate by inhibiting hepatic and intestinal CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid coadministration or use an alternative drug. 12. Miconazole vaginal increases the levels or effects of erythromycin stearate by inhibiting hepatic and intestinal CYP3A4 metabolism. This combination is contraindicated. 13. Erythromycin stearate decreases the effects of oral microbiota by pharmacodynamic antagonism. Avoid coadministration or use an alternative drug. Complete antibiotic regimens 2–4 days before initiating oral microbiota therapy. 14. Erythromycin stearate increases the levels or effects of midazolam (oral and intranasal) by inhibiting hepatic and intestinal CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid coadministration or use an alternative drug. Coadministration with moderate CYP3A4 inhibitors may prolong sedation. 15. Erythromycin stearate increases the levels or effects of mifepristone by inhibiting hepatic and intestinal CYP3A4 metabolism. Both drugs prolong the QTc interval. Avoid coadministration or use an alternative drug. 16. Erythromycin stearate and mipomersen both increase hepatic enzyme levels. Use caution and monitor liver function tests (LFTs). 17. Erythromycin stearate and mirtazapine both prolong the QTc interval. Avoid coadministration or use an alternative drug. 18. Mitotane decreases erythromycin stearate levels by inducing hepatic and intestinal CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor closely. Mitotane is a strong CYP3A4 inducer, so dosage adjustments may be necessary. 19. Erythromycin stearate increases the levels or effects of mitoxantrone by inhibiting P-glycoprotein (MDR1) efflux transporters. Use caution and monitor closely. 20. Erythromycin stearate increases the levels of mizolastine by decreasing its metabolism. This combination is contraindicated. 21. Erythromycin stearate increases the toxicity of momelotinib by inhibiting OATP1B1/B3 transporters. Use caution and monitor closely for adverse reactions. 22. Erythromycin stearate increases the levels or effects of montelukast by inhibiting hepatic and intestinal CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor closely. 23. Erythromycin stearate and moxifloxacin both prolong the QTc interval. Avoid coadministration or use an alternative drug. 24. Nafcillin decreases erythromycin stearate levels by inducing hepatic and intestinal CYP3A4 metabolism. Erythromycin stearate decreases nafcillin effects by pharmacodynamic antagonism. Monitor closely. 25. Erythromycin stearate increases the levels or effects of naloxegol by inhibiting hepatic and intestinal CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid coadministration or use an alternative drug. 26. Nefazodone increases erythromycin stearate levels by inhibiting hepatic and intestinal CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid coadministration or use an alternative drug. 27. Erythromycin stearate increases the levels or effects of nelfinavir by inhibiting P-glycoprotein (MDR1) efflux transporters and hepatic CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid coadministration or use an alternative drug. 28. Erythromycin stearate increases the levels or effects of neomycin by inhibiting P-glycoprotein (MDR1) efflux transporters. Use caution and monitor closely. 29. Erythromycin stearate increases the levels or effects of neratinib by inhibiting hepatic and intestinal CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid coadministration or use an alternative drug. 30. Nevirapine decreases erythromycin stearate levels by inducing hepatic and intestinal CYP3A4 metabolism. This combination is contraindicated. 31. Erythromycin stearate decreases niacin levels by altering intestinal flora. Use caution and monitor closely. 32. Erythromycin stearate increases the levels or effects of nicardipine by inhibiting hepatic and intestinal CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid coadministration or use an alternative drug. 33. Erythromycin stearate increases the levels or effects of nifedipine by inhibiting hepatic and intestinal CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor closely. Initiate nifedipine at the lowest dose if coadministered. 34. Erythromycin stearate increases the levels or effects of nilotinib by inhibiting P-glycoprotein (MDR1) efflux transporters and hepatic CYP3A4 metabolism. Both drugs prolong the QTc interval. Avoid coadministration or use an alternative drug. 35. Nilutamide increases erythromycin stearate levels by inhibiting hepatic and intestinal CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid coadministration or use an alternative drug. 36. Erythromycin stearate increases the levels or effects of nimodipine by inhibiting hepatic and intestinal CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor closely. 37. Erythromycin stearate increases the levels of nintedanib by inhibiting P-glycoprotein (MDR1) efflux transporters. Therapy modification or close monitoring is required. Manage adverse effects with dose adjustments or therapy discontinuation. 38. Nirmatrelvir increases erythromycin stearate levels by inhibiting hepatic and intestinal CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor for increased adverse effects, including QTc prolongation. 39. Erythromycin stearate increases the levels or effects of nisoldipine by inhibiting hepatic and intestinal CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid coadministration or use an alternative drug. 40. Erythromycin stearate increases the levels or effects of nitrenedipine by inhibiting hepatic and intestinal CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor closely. 41. Erythromycin stearate increases the levels or effects of norgestrel by inhibiting hepatic and intestinal CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor closely. Strong or moderate CYP3A4 inhibitors may increase systemic norgestrel concentrations, raising the risk of adverse effects. 42. Erythromycin stearate and nortriptyline both prolong the QTc interval. Avoid coadministration or use an alternative drug. 43. Erythromycin stearate and octreotide both prolong the QTc interval. Avoid coadministration or use an alternative drug. 44. Erythromycin stearate and ofloxacin both prolong the QTc interval. Therapy modification or close monitoring is required. 45. Erythromycin stearate and olanzapine both prolong the QTc interval. Avoid coadministration or use an alternative drug. 46. Erythromycin stearate increases the levels or effects of olaparib by inhibiting hepatic and intestinal CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid coadministration or use an alternative drug. If unavoidable, reduce olaparib dose and monitor closely. 47. Erythromycin stearate increases the levels or effects of oliceridine by inhibiting hepatic and intestinal CYP3A4 metabolism. Therapy modification or close monitoring is required. Adjust oliceridine dosing and monitor for respiratory depression and sedation. 48. Erythromycin stearate and olodaterol both prolong the QTc interval. Use caution and monitor closely. Increased risk of ventricular arrhythmias may occur. 49. Erythromycin stearate increases the levels or effects of omaveloxolone by inhibiting hepatic and intestinal CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid coadministration or use an alternative drug. If unavoidable, reduce omaveloxolone dose and monitor closely. 50. Erythromycin stearate and ondansetron both prolong the QTc interval. Avoid coadministration or use an alternative drug. ECG monitoring is recommended in high-risk patients. 51. Erythromycin stearate and osilodrostat both prolong the QTc interval. Use caution and monitor closely. 52. Erythromycin stearate and osimertinib both prolong the QTc interval. Avoid coadministration or use an alternative drug. If unavoidable, monitor closely for adverse effects. 53. Erythromycin stearate decreases oxacillin effects by pharmacodynamic antagonism. Monitor closely.
